title: How can communication experts incorporate AI into their daily work?
summary: A concise reflection on ethical, culturally relevant AI use in communication and adult learning, with people and local realities kept at the centre.

author.name: Joseph Masonda
author.role: Communications Officer | Digital Marketer | Website Designer | Content Creator | AI Enthusiast | Framer Developer | Writer

coverImage.note: Add a locally hosted cover image before publishing.

content.text: AI is here to stay. There is no need to fight it.
AI offers many ways to support communications professionals, but without a human touch and a strong idea, even the smartest AI can fall flat.

After attending an online webinar hosted by the UNESCO Institute for Lifelong Learning on lifelong learning in the age of AI, one key lesson stood out: AI must be contextualised to better suit adult educators as they learn and adapt.
It is not about replacing teachers. It is about amplifying culture, values and community needs.
Technology is often treated as a silver bullet. Yet, in communication and adult learning, it still needs to be woven into the social fabric and tailored to local realities and each area of expertise.
Let it simplify your work, while you solve the challenges.

items: Use AI tools ethically and adapt them to community norms, literacy levels and languages.
Make sure results are accessible and benefit communities, including lessons, messages and visuals that are useful to them.
Recognise when human connection is necessary to achieve the best results.

content.text: AI should be used to create ethical, culturally relevant solutions that put people first. The focus must shift from flashy technology to meaningful impact.
How are you integrating local culture into your technology solutions without losing your human essence?
